result.title: Human Capital in Context: What Employment Survival Reveals About Worker-Firm Match
result.summary: There is no best worker in general, only a best worker for a particular firm. We develop a measure of worker-firm match quality that treats fit as a property of the pair, learned from the survival of employment relationships. A two-tower neural network embeds workers, from their career histories and current positions, and firms, from their characteristics and business descriptions, into a common space, and match quality is the cosine similarity of the two vectors. The measure takes its functional form from the skill-weights model of firm-specific human capital, and its only estimated objective, a separation hazard, from the view of the job match as an experience good. Estimated on more than a billion person-periods covering 101 million workers and 8.4 million firms, a 0.1 increase in match quality lowers the odds of separation by 48%. About a quarter of the variance of match quality is specific to the worker-firm pair, which worker-, firm-, and occupation-level measures set to zero by construction. Workers earn more when better matched, especially early in a relationship, and firms whose workforces score higher grow faster, become more profitable, and are issued more, and more valuable, patents over the next five years than their industry peers. Because it scores pairs that never formed, the measure also predicts where movers go, and acquirers record a larger share of the price as goodwill when the target's workers would fit the acquirer better than they fit the target.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出以雇佣关系存续为监督信号学习「人—企业匹配质量」：用双塔网络把员工职业史与企业特征嵌入同一空间，以余弦相似度定义匹配度，并以离职风险为唯一估计目标，在十亿级人—期数据上估计；发现约四分之一匹配质量方差为配对方特有，且高匹配与更高薪酬、企业成长和专利产出相关。
